stories.headline: Several injured in Australia as car crashes into crowd north of Sydney
stories.deck: The driver was arrested ‌at the scene in the ‌city about 110 km (68 ‌miles) ⁠north of the ⁠New South Wales state capital, Sydney
stories.bodyText:
Australian officials say a car drove into a large crowd standing on a road to cheer on the Newcastle Knights rugby team north of Sydney, injuring multiple people.
The driver was arrested at the scene in the city about 110 km (68 miles) north of the New South Wales state capital, Sydney.
Authorities could not confirm how many people had been injured, a police spokesperson said, adding that initial indications suggested the incident was not terrorism-related.
Multiple people, including children, were critically injured, Newcastle Mayor Gavin Morris said in televised remarks.
Thousands had lined the city’s streets to farewell the Newcastle Knights rugby league team due to compete in the country’s National Rugby League grand final in Sydney on Sunday (October 4, 2026), the Australian Broadcasting Corp reported.
(With inputs from AP and Reuters)

stories.headline: Gaza war could have ended a year earlier, says ex Israeli hostage negotiator
stories.deck: Major General Nitzan Alon revealed that the Gaza war could have been concluded a year prior. He argued that an earlier resolution would have spared the lives of countless hostages and civilians. Alon criticized the prevailing notion that total victory over Hamas had to be accomplished before any negotiations, asserting this approach was flawed.
stories.bodyText:
Former Israeli hostage negotiator Major General (retd) Nitzan Alon has said Israel could have ended the Gaza war about a year earlier and secured the release of all its remaining hostages without significantly compromising its other strategic objectives.
According to Al Jazeera, Alon made the remarks during a Washington Institute for Near East Policy webcast on October 2, arguing that Israel could have reached the position it ultimately achieved “much earlier, maybe a year earlier or so”. He said the prolonged war may have cost the lives of hostages who could otherwise have been brought home alive.
Alon, who served as the Israeli military's point person for hostage negotiations during the war, said Israel's insistence on achieving “total victory” over Hamas before accepting a comprehensive deal was based on a false premise.
He argued that the October 2025 ceasefire and hostage agreement demonstrated that Israel could have achieved its broader strategic objectives while reaching a deal much earlier.
Alon said the decision to continue the war also had a human cost, arguing that an earlier agreement could have brought some hostages home alive and potentially saved thousands of lives on both sides.
He said Israel “could have and should have” shortened the war and returned the hostages earlier.
The October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas came into effect on October 10, 2025, under a US-backed plan aimed at ending the Gaza war and securing the release of the remaining Israeli hostages.
Under the first phase of the deal, Hamas agreed to release all 20 living Israeli hostages, while Israel agreed to release Palestinian prisoners and detainees and withdraw its forces to agreed positions in Gaza.
The October 2025 deal came nearly two years after the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel, in which 251 people were abducted and taken to Gaza.
The attack killed more than 1,200 people, according to Israeli figures, triggering Israel’s military campaign in Gaza and a prolonged effort to secure the release of the hostages.

stories.headline: Salman Khan praises hero pilot Smit Machchhar: 'Well done bro'
stories.deck: Salman Khan shared his appreciation for Captain Smit Machchhar's efforts in saving lives during a flight incident. The pilot was attacked by his co-pilot while flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv and sustained serious injuries. Despite this, he managed to successfully land the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia with over 170 people on board. Other Indian celebrities, including Shilpa Shetty and Jackie…
stories.bodyText:
Bollywood's bhaijaan, 
Salman Khan
 has become the latest celebrity to laud Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who helped save over 100 lives on a FlyDubai flight.
Taking to his X handle, Salman shared a message of appreciation for Machchhar, who was seriously injured when he was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot mid-air. In his tweet, Khan wrote, “Kamaal kar diya pilot ji, hum sab aap ko salute karte hain will be a pleasure to fly with u.. Well done bro.. Capt #SmitMachchhar."
As per reports, Machchhar was piloting FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30 when the co-pilot allegedly attacked him inside the cockpit. Despite sustaining injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, after which passengers and crew members entered the cockpit and helped restrain the attacker.
The aircraft was eventually diverted and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. As per a report on Reuters, more than 170 people were on board, and all occupants reached safety.
Salman is among several Indian celebrities to publicly acknowledge Machchhar’s heroism. Shilpa Shetty also posted, “Heart goes out to everyone affected. And immense respect for Captain Smit Machchhar for bringing over 170 lives to safety.”
Actor Jackie Shroff also praised the pilot saying, “Some heroes work in silence! All my respects to Captain Smit Machchhar and the other brave heroes for saving lives and averting a massive tragedy.”
On the work front, Salman Khan is currently shooting for 'Bigg Boss' and is also shooting his action entertainer directed by Vamshi Paidipally, co-starring Nayanthara. He is also awaiting the release of his war film, 'Maatrubhumi' which is still awaiting its release.

stories.headline: FlyDubai co-pilot who nearly crashed plane was barred from flying by Oman over extremism concerns
stories.deck: The attack left the region’s travel industry in crisis, raising questions about aviation security and further unsettling West Asia, already shaken by the U.S.-Iran war
stories.bodyText:
The FlyDubai co-pilot who officials said nearly crashed a Tel Aviv-bound flight with 182 people aboard was barred from flying by his native Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views, a person familiar with the matter said Saturday.
The co-pilot was subsequently hired by the United Arab Emirates-based airline, the person said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing investigation. It was not immediately clear to what extent he was vetted when he was hired in the Emirates. Oman’s move to bar the co-pilot from flying was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.
The attack left the region’s travel industry in crisis, raising questions about aviation security and further unsettling West Asia, already shaken by the U.S.-Iran war. A regional investigation is underway.
The United Arab Emirates has canceled all flights to Israel, complicating travel for hundreds of passengers who fly between the countries on a typical day. Israel and the UAE agreed on repatriation flights, beginning Friday (October 2, 2026), to bring back passengers stranded in the UAE after commercial travel between the two countries was suspended, according to an Israeli official who was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.
The first repatriation flight left the UAE shortly before 11 p.m. and landed in Tel Aviv just after 1 a.m., according to the Ben Gurion International Airport website.
The airport listed carriers Arkia and Israir with flights scheduled to arrive from Dubai early Saturday. El Al was expected to fly passengers from Dubai to Israel on Sunday (October 4, 2026).
Dubai has been a popular destination for Israelis since Israel and the UAE established ties in 2020 as part of the Trump administration’s Abraham Accords to normalize ties between Israel and Arab countries.
Attacks raise questions about extremism
U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters that early information he’s received suggests links between the attack and Tehran but did not elaborate. Mr. Trump also said that if it is determined that Iranian agents were behind the attack, the United States will “hit them very hard.”
Israeli investigators are involved in the probe, but the Emiratis are in the lead, according to an official who wasn’t authorized to speak to the media and spoke on condition of anonymity. It’s unclear if the attacker was part of a group, said the official, adding that there is currently no evidence of a link with Iran.
“We are now investigating whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a video message on Friday (October 2, 2026).
UAE senior diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash on Friday (October 2, 2026) called the FlyDubai attack a “dangerous terrorist act” in a post on X. He credited the flight captain for preventing a catastrophe.
The moment is a test for the UAE government, which has burnished a reputation for building effective measures against extremist activities but has also bristled in the past over criticism of security lapses.
“The Emiratis are going to be interested in protecting their reputation,” said Jon Alterman, chair of Global Security and Geostrategy at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington. “They believe people should see them as a place that’s very secure, not a place that has serious lapses.”
The FlyDubai flight plummeted to 15,000 feet
Details of the harrowing flight, in which other crew members on board landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday (September 30, 2026), continue to emerge.
Smit Machchhar, the wounded captain who has been hailed as one of the heroes of the flight, and the co-pilot were transferred on Thursday (October 1, 2026) from Saudi Arabia to the UAE, the kingdom said.
Machchhar is recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital. He spoke with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a televised video call Friday, describing the terror he faced after being attacked in the closed cockpit.
“I had so many wounds. I had fallen down,” he said, his head bandaged, as he broke into sobs. “I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realized that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.”
The first signs of trouble came more than two hours into the flight when the aircraft suddenly dropped to 16,600 feet — the sharpest altitude drop recorded by data tracking platforms. But moments before the nosedive, passengers seated near the front of the plane heard sounds of a fight inside the cockpit, said passenger Daniel Schlichter, who was seated in the second row.
Seconds later, it ascended to 21,725 feet before soon dropping back to 15,000 feet, which it maintained until safely landing more than an hour later.

stories.bodyText: Cairo: An Israeli airstrike killed at least five Palestinians in an apartment building in Gaza City early on Saturday, health and civil defense service officials said. briefs.headline: Dalit woman ‘denied’ hospital admission over caste, gives birth by UP roadside
briefs.deck: A 20-year-old woman from the Dalit Mushar community faced denial of admission at a government hospital in Uttar Pradesh. After being refused care due to her caste, she gave birth on the roadside with family assistance. The incident prompted immediate disciplinary action against the medical staff involved in her case. A four-member inquiry panel found negligence from multiple hospital personnel…
briefs.bodyText:
VARANASI: A woman from the Dalit Mushar community, allegedly denied admission to a govt hospital in Uttar Pradesh’s Bhadohi because of her caste, gave birth in a public area outside the health facility, leading to dismissal of the on-duty doctor and action against others.
Deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak, who is also in-charge of health department, took serious note of the issue after a video of the incident was widely circulated online.
The woman, Rani (20), was brought to Maharaja Chet Singh District Hospital in Gyanpur Tuesday night after she went into labour. Her family alleged that hospital staff refused to admit her after identifying her as Musahar. While leaving the hospital, Rani’s condition worsened. Her family helped her deliver the baby on the roadside.
Later, CMO Dr SK Chak got the mother and the newborn admitted to the hospital and ordered an inquiry.
Following the findings of the four-member panel, EMO Dr Pankaj was sacked, staff nurse Neelam Maurya was transferred, and the salary of obstetrician Dr Mukesh Prajapati was withheld. A recommendation has also been sent to the state govt for action against CMS Dr Ajay Tiwari and Dr Neelima Dhawan.
As per the inquiry report, Dr Pankaj, who was on duty when Rani arrived, referred her without examination; while Dr Dhawan had reportedly examined Rani a day earlier but referred her elsewhere instead of admitting her, despite her severe anaemia. The CMS, too, was found to have been negligent in handling the case.
Dr Prajapati was found to have been outside the district at the time and had reached the hospital about one-and-a-half hours later. And the nurse had allegedly refused her admission while referring to the family as Musahar.

briefs.headline: Vande Bharat crosses Chenab, Anji bridges at 100 kmph as Katra-Banihal train speed limit raised
briefs.deck: He said the Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) created a new record by crossing both the world's highest Chenab Bridge and India's first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at 100 kmph
briefs.bodyText:
A Vande Bharat Express crossed the world's highest railway bridge over the Chenab River and India's first cable-stayed railway bridge at Anji at 100 kmph, as the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Katra-Banihal broad-gauge rail section was raised to 100 kmph, officials said.
The speed enhancement on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section under the Jammu division of Northern Railway was successfully tested on Thursday (October 1, 2026) , marking a significant operational milestone for the ambitious Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Link (USBRL) project.
"The maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph," senior divisional commercial manager Uchit Singhal said.
He said the Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) created a new record by crossing both the world's highest Chenab Bridge and India's first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at 100 kmph.
The 111-km Katra-Banihal section is a crucial and technically challenging component of the USBRL project, which is aimed at providing seamless rail connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of the country.
The Railway Ministry approved the enhancement in the maximum permissible speed to 100 kmph after all prescribed safety conditions were complied with by the Railways in August this year, officials said.
Earlier, trains were permitted to operate at a maximum speed of 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section.
The increase in the permissible speed is expected to make train operations on the USBRL project smoother, reduce travel time and provide faster, safer and more comfortable journeys to passengers.
With the enhancement, travel time between Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra and Banihal is also expected to come down, providing faster and more comfortable rail connectivity in the region.
The Katra-Banihal section traverses some of the most difficult and rugged terrain of the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, involving deep valleys, steep mountain slopes, major rivers and highly complex geological formations.
The construction of the line has therefore required extensive use of advanced engineering techniques, including long tunnels, high-level bridges and sophisticated railway infrastructure, officials said.
The section has some of the country's most prestigious and challenging engineering structures, including the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world's highest railway bridge, constructed over the Chenab River near Reasi, and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge, India's first cable-stayed railway bridge.
The section also has 33 tunnels.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra on June 6, 2025.

briefs.headline: North Korea fires ballistic missile toward sea, South Korea and Japan say
briefs.bodyText: Seoul: North Korea fired a ballistic missile toward the sea off its east coast on Saturday, South Korea and Japan said. The missile was launched from the Wonsan area at around 6.30 a.m. on Saturday (2130 GMT, Friday), the South Korean military said in a statement. It did not elaborate on how far the missile flew. Japan's coast guard, in an emailed statement citing the Japanese defence ministry, said the object may have been a ballistic missile and appeared to have come down, warning ships to take precautions. South Korea's military said it has raised its monitoring of any further missile tests and will share intelligence with the US and Japan. .Ukraine's Zelenskyy says North Korea prepares to deploy another 10,000 troops to Russia. The South Korean presidential office's national security council convened an emergency meeting on Saturday to assess the situation after the missile launch, the office said in a statement. The launch came after Pyongyang's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, issued a statement on Friday that dismissed Seoul's demand for an apology for what it said were North Korean mines that seriously wounded South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarised Zone, a heavily fortified area between the two Koreas. South Korea said this week that North Korean mines caused the blast that seriously injured two South Korean soldiers on a reconnaissance mission inside the 4-km-wide (2.5-mile) border that stretches across the Korean Peninsula. North Korea has sharply ramped up hostility against the South in recent years, disavowing unification as a national goal and calling South Korea its "primary foe".

briefs.headline: Flydubai co-pilot identified; was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
briefs.bodyText:
The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.
Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.
Removed from Oman Air training role
The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.
Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings
Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.
According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.
Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight
The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.
An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.
Who is Hamam Alhamami?
According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.
CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.
Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.
What happened aboard flydubai flight
The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.
The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.
Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.
Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.

briefs.headline: DIY crafts using socks
briefs.deck: DIY crafts using socks
briefs.bodyText: Ask an adult to help with all the cutting and sewing. Never use scissors or needles without adult supervision. . Hello hare . Materials needed . *2 old socks . *Cotton wool or clean fabric scraps for stuffing . *Googly eyes . *A black marker . *Small pieces of felt or fabric for the nose and spots . *Glue . *Thread and needle . Method . 1) To make the body, fill one sock with cotton wool or fabric scraps until it is round and plump. An adult can sew the opening shut. . 2) Make the head by stuffing the second sock with cotton wool or fabric scraps to make a smaller, round shape. Sew the opening closed. . 3) With an adult’s help, cut two long, pointed ear shapes from the remaining part of the sock. Sew or glue them to the top of the head. . 4) To add a face, stick on two googly eyes, draw a small nose, and a smiling mouth with a black marker. . 5) Cut small circles from pink or coloured felt and glue them onto the body for the spots. You can choose any colours you like. . 6) Securely sew or glue the head onto the body. . Puppet fun . Materials needed . *1 old, clean sock . *Wool or yarn for the hair . *2 buttons or googly eyes . *Glue . *A piece of felt for the mouth, if you like . Method . 1) Pick a clean sock that fits comfortably over your hand. . 2) To make the hair, cut several pieces of wool or yarn of the same length. Glue the strands to the top of the sock to make hair. . 3) For the eyes, glue two buttons or googly eyes onto the sock. Let the glue dry completely. . 4) You can draw a mouth with a marker or glue on a small piece of felt to make one. . 5) Add a bow, ribbon or other small decorations to create your own character. . 6) Slip your hand inside the sock and make your puppet talk, sing or tell a story!

stories.headline: Amid threat, Karnataka govt releases contractors’ Rs 2,400 crore dues
stories.deck: Karnataka's government has released Rs 2,400 crore to the irrigation department over the past few days. This release addresses a small fraction of the pending Rs 38,000 crore in bills owed to contractors. The contractors' association claims that the government's efforts are insufficient and have minimal impact on accruing loans. A senior government official mentioned plans to clear dues of Public…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Amid protest threats by contractors’ association over Rs 38,000 crore in pending bills, Karnataka govt has released Rs 2,400 crore to the irrigation department over the past three days.
The association had written to the CM two days ago even as govt had set aside Rs 1,400 crore for clearing pending bills in irrigation department that has highest dues.
Contractors said the release covers less than 10% of dues and ad-hoc measure has no real impact on loans piling up. R Manjunath, association president, said “What is the use if payments are made once in 3-4 months? They should clear the amount in one single stroke and do whatever they please later.”
A senior govt official said that finance department will issue an NOC for the purpose and added that a similar exercise may be taken up to clear dues of PWD contractors.
No additional provision to clear dues, say officials
Govt has decided to release next quarter’s funds early, allowing departments to use part of the allocation to clear pending bills while continuing ongoing work.
“Departments can use the funds judiciously and maintain a balance between expenditure for current work and pending bills,” said an official.
Officials said govt cannot go beyond existing budgetary allocations and that there will be no additional provision to clear dues.
Manjunath said the CMO has sought a meeting with the association and alleged that the Rs 1,400 crore earmarked for irrigation bills would be paid out based on seniority, benefiting bigger contractors and leaving smaller contractors waiting.
The association puts pending bills at Rs 13,000 crore for major and medium irrigation, Rs 8,370 crore for PWD, Rs 3,800 crore for RDPR and Rs 3,000 crore for minor irrigation. Officials said these figures may include estimates for ongoing work.

stories.headline: Back from movie, Bengaluru man finds house ransacked and gets attacked by robbers
stories.deck: A 31-year-old man named P Jagadish returned home to find it ransacked after a movie outing. He confronted two intruders, one masked and one wearing a helmet, who attacked him. The assailants fled with gold and silver jewelry valued at approximately 20 grams and 45 grams, respectively. Jagadish suffered a deep head injury during the confrontation and sought help from neighbors.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A late-night movie outing turned horrific for a 31-year-old man after he returned to his house around 1.30am on Sept 26 and found it ransacked. Worse, two intruders still inside the house attacked him before scooting away with 20 grams of gold jewellery and 45 grams of silver ornaments.
According to a complaint filed by P Jagadish, from Maruthi Layout in Katamnallur, his family had travelled to Andhra Pradesh on Sept 25. Jagadish, who works in the finance department at a private hospital in Hoskote, stayed back in Bengaluru. He and his friends planned a movie night out.
After returning from work, he locked his house around 10.15pm and left for the theatre. Upon his return, Jagadish was aghast to find the front door of his house ajar. According to his complaint, one intruder was tall and thin and wearing a helmet, and the other was of average height and had covered his face with a mask. He suspects the miscreants were aged between 25 and 30 years.
As Jagadish confronted them, the masked miscreant struck him on the head with an iron rod. As they tried to attack him again, Jagadish rushed out and sought help from neighbours. In the melee, the duo fled on a bike.
Jagadish found gold jewellery, including a pair of earrings, a chain and six finger rings, missing from the cupboard. The thieves also made off with two silver waist belts, a pair of bangles and three pairs of anklets. Jagadish, bleeding from a deep head injury, informed his friends about the incident. He was taken to a hospital, from where he has since been discharged.

stories.headline: Karnataka CM questions removal of Gandhi’s name from NREGA scheme
stories.bodyText:
Expressing displeasure over the Union government changing the name of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme to Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said, “When Gandhiji was killed, almost all member nations of the United Nation Organisation (UNO) lowered their flags to half-mast as a mark of respect. Yet, it remains incomprehensible why the Union government removed Gandhiji’s name from the employment guarantee scheme.”
The Chief Minister questioned, “What harm would be in retaining Gandhiji’s name in the NREGA scheme?” He asserted that there is a need for a detailed discussion on this matter.
Mr. Shivakumar was speaking at a ceremony held in Gandhi Bhavan on Friday, after presenting Gandhi Seva Award-2026 and Gandhi Puraskar to 11 addiction-free villages in Koppal district.
“There are two ideologies in this country: one is the family that embraces Gandhian principles, and the other is the group that opposes Gandhism. The nation is witnessing a conflict between the two. All of us who follow Gandhian principles belong to the Gandhi family. Our government is walking the path of his ideology,” Mr. Shivakumar said.
Meanwhile, Woode P. Krishna, recipient of the Gandhi Seva Award, emphasised the need to convey Gandhiji’s ideals to the younger generation, noting that there are systematic attempts to misinterpret the Mahatma.
The prize money of ₹5 lakh was donated to the Karnataka Gandhi Smaraka Nidhi.
‘Gandhi Puraskara’ was presented to eleven villages in Koppal district that voluntarily became free of liquor sales, and to the ‘Gandhi Balaga’ of Koppal, an organisation working to preach Gandhi’s principles in rural areas.
The State Alcohol Temperance Board honoured villages including Hatti, Lebageri, Talakanakapura, Hanumanahalli, Kamanuru, Binnala and Chikkenakoppa in Kukanoor taluk, and Madnala, Nagarala, Boduru Tanda, and Hirebannigola in Kushtagi taluk for making villages free from alcohol sales. The award package included a ‘Charkha’ (spinning wheel) and a book.
RWF takes Swatchhata pledge
General Manager, Manoranjan Pradhan, with other officers and staff of Rail Wheel Factory (RWF), celebrated Gandhi Jayanti by taking Swatchhata pledge.
As a part of Swatchhata Hi Seva Abhiyaan (SHS) 2026, Swatchhata Pakhwara is being observed at the RWF from October 1 to 15. Various activities including shramadaan, health screening camps, intensive cleanliness drives at various locations on the factory premises and colonies, workshop on doll making out of waste cloth, were held at the RWF.

stories.headline: SIR amounts to ‘vote theft’, say protesters in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Demanding the resignation and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar for making “massive and unprecedented changes to voter databases”, members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) staged a protest in Bengaluru on Friday as part of a nationwide agitation seeking action against the CEC.
The protesters argued that key decisions relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were pushed through under Mr. Kumar without the authorisation or approval of the other two Election Commissioners, even when the Commissioners had objected to the changes, describing them as “unauthorised and illegal”.
The protesters said that if Mr. Kumar did not resign, they would intensify the agitation and reach out to Opposition parties to press for impeachment proceedings against the CEC in Parliament.
Pointing to an unprecedented scale of deletions, AISA members said more than 13 crore names had been excluded from the draft rolls across States where the SIR was conducted. They argued that the exercise was being driven by the BJP’s “fascist politics” and was aimed at retaining its (BJP) voter base while excluding minority communities, describing the exercise akin to “ethnic cleansing”.
AISA demanded that the SIR be scrapped immediately and that States where the exercise had resulted in deletions restore the electoral rolls that existed before the revision – to the January 2025 rolls. It also sought criminal action against Mr. Kumar, accusing him of “institutional corruption” and intentional “vote theft” involving crores of citizens.
The protesters also demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, pointing that the two Election Commissioners had approached the Cabinet Secretary over their objections to the SIR-related decisions, and that the Union government was therefore aware of the concerns but had failed to act on them.
Condemning the detention of protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, including AISA national president Neha Bora and activist Yogendra Yadav, the protesters here said that the BJP government had become increasingly authoritarian in dealing with dissent. They said dissenters were being treated as “second-class citizens” and warned that the youth would continue to protest until a fundamental overhaul of the electoral system and its institutions was carried out.

briefs.headline: Winning the medal was special but there was no time to celebrate: Tilottama Sen
briefs.deck: Bengaluru’s Tilottama Sen on winning her first Asian Games medal and finding her feet as a Gen Z athlete
briefs.bodyText:
For Bengaluru’s Tilottama Sen, winning a silver medal at the Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 was a moment she will remember for a long time. The 18-year-old, along with Vidarsa Vinod and Ashi Chouksey, won silver in the women’s 50m rifle 3-positions team event, marking her first medal at a continental competition. Yet, there was little time to celebrate. The team discovered they had won silver just before Tilottama had to compete in the individual final. “We were excited, but we didn’t really get the time to celebrate because I had my final immediately after that. It was great to win a medal in my debut Asian Games. I was really happy about it,” she says.
For a young athlete competing on such a big stage, expectations can often feel overwhelming. Tilottama, however, says she has learnt to approach competitions without letting pressure take over. “I have my own expectations, and my parents do too, but I have never taken them as pressure. My only goal at the Asian Games was to execute what I had learnt from my previous two international competitions and correct the mistakes I had made,” she says.
‘I have learnt not to hold on to mistakes’
While the team silver was a moment of celebration, finishing fourth in the individual final gave Tilottama plenty to reflect on. 
“After my match, I sat down and spoke to my coach about what had happened. There were things I still had to work on. My coach told me to accept what had happened, but not hold on to it for too long. I realised that holding on to things would not let me move forward,” she says.
She is now focused on addressing those mistakes before her next competition.
‘People are noticing shooting more now’
Shooting has steadily gained attention in India, particularly after the country’s performances at recent international competitions. Tilottama feels the sport is reaching a wider audience, with more people recognising the achievements of Indian shooters. “I would say a lot of people were not aware of the sport until the last Olympic Games, when Manu Bhaker won two medals. Since then, shooting has been getting noticed,” she says.
She also believes that India’s growing sporting ecosystem could open up opportunities for more young athletes. “We have schemes coming up to help grassroots-level athletes. I am sure that in the coming years, many more athletes and talents will emerge,” she says.
‘Gen Z athletes have more hunger to do something bigger and better’
At 18, Tilottama is part of a generation of athletes making their mark on the international stage at a young age. “More Gen Z athletes are coming up because we have the opportunities and facilities from the very beginning. Another reason is that they have that hunger to do something big or do something better. That is why we are seeing a lot of young athletes across sports,” she says.

briefs.headline: From kodubale to filter coffee, Bengaluru gets a taste of nostalgia
briefs.bodyText:
What makes a South Indian celebration memorable? It could be the crunch of freshly made kodubale, a ragi laddoo passed around, filter coffee poured into a davara tumbler, or the rituals that bring communities together. Bengaluru recently brought these familiar flavours and traditions to The Big South Indian Festival – a celebration of regional food, stories and culture. While food took centre stage at this festival, experiences such as storytelling, games, Yakshagana performances and activities took people back to their childhood.
‘Celebration has never been just about one thing’
Food historian Rakesh Raghunathan, who was part of the festival, says the mix of food, music, games, and rituals reflects how celebrations have traditionally unfolded across South India. “Celebration has never been just about one thing. It has always been around art, culture, food, music, games, rituals, and of course, storytelling — all of these have seamlessly co-existed,” he says.
‘Food connects us to the memory’
“Food has that unique ability to transport us. There's a familiar taste, an aroma, or even the way something is served that can take you back to a person or a particular place. Across South India, every dish, every spoonful of what we savour has a story: the story of communities, seasonal eating, rituals, and the whole migration of how those recipes have evolved and travelled, along with generations of knowledge that have been passed down. This is really what makes food such a powerful connector. So when we share food, we're not just sharing something to eat; we're sharing a part of our memory and our identity as we do that,” shares Rakesh.

briefs.headline: Eastward ho! Hoskote, 30km from Bengaluru, to be next transport gateway
briefs.deck: Metro Extension, High-Speed Rail Corridors & B’luru-Chennai Expressway Converging Around Satellite Town
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Hoskote, an urban outback not long ago and now a bustling suburb some 30km on the eastern flank of Bengaluru, is emerging as a key transport gateway to the tech capital, with a proposed Metro extension, high-speed rail corridors and Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway converging around the eastern satellite town.
BMRCL is preparing a DPR for a 17-km Metro line from KR Pura to Hoskote, adding another public transport link to a corridor already seeing rapid growth in road and rail infrastructure.
Hoskote MLA Sharath Kumar Bache Gowda, who attended a meeting on the proposed extension in the presence of chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
, said: “The CM has given the green signal for the project. Once the DPR is ready, steps will be initiated to take up the project.”
A feasibility report has estimated Metro project’s Economic Internal Rate of Return (EIRR) around 19%, Sharath said, indicating the project’s potential viability as a mass-transit corridor.
On the other hand, the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway is partially operational, with the roughly 100-km Hoskote-Baireddipalle (Andhra Pradesh) section currently open. Other sections are yet to become operational.
Hoskote is also proposed to have an integrated station for the Bengaluru-Chennai and Bengaluru-Hyderabad high-speed rail corridors. 
A depot, workshops and operations control centre have been proposed at Kodihalli, near Hoskote, as part of the high-speed rail infrastructure.
Authorities are also considering transit-oriented development around the town, including a proposal to acquire about 80 hectares for transport-related infrastructure.
The growing road traffic is adding urgency to the debate over how the KR Pura-Hoskote corridor should be developed. Traffic volumes on NH-75 have crossed 80,000 passenger car units (PCUs), even before the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway becomes fully operational.
Once the expressway is fully operational, pressure on the Hoskote-KR Pura stretch is expected to increase. The proposed Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR) connection towards Hosur Road could add further traffic movement, with vehicles from Bengaluru potentially using both routes.
Those advocating additional road capacity estimate traffic could cross 1.5 lakh PCUs in the coming years. They argue that a double-decker structure could separate through traffic from local movements and provide better integration with the STRR.
The idea, however, remains contentious. Earlier proposals envisaged a road flyover at the lower level and Metro on the upper level. Critics question whether combining road capacity with a mass-transit project could undermine prioritising public transport.
BMRCL faced similar concerns over double-decker stretches on the Orange Line. Following a RITES study and opposition from several quarters, it reduced the proposed double-decker section from 37 km to 11 km.
Supporters of a double-decker structure on the Hoskote stretch argue that its traffic conditions are different because of existing congestion and the expected convergence of expressway and STRR traffic.
NHAI is already operating an 83-km stretch of Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR), connecting Dabaspet to Hoskote via Doddaballapur and Devanahalli. The operational stretch is integrated with Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway at Hoskote.
Earlier, NHAI had also proposed widening NH 75 into a 10-lane road from the expressway’s cloverleaf interchange at Hoskote.
Hoskote’s Emerging Transport Network
■ Metro: A proposed 17-km KR Pura-Hoskote Metro line is being taken up for DPR preparation
■ Expressway: Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway is partially operational. The Hoskote-Baireddipalle stretch of about 100 km is currently open
■ High-speed rail: An integrated station is proposed at Hoskote for the Bengaluru-Chennai and Bengaluru-Hyderabad high-speed rail corridors
■ Rail facilities: A depot, workshops and operations control centre are proposed at Kodihalli near Hoskote
■ Transit-oriented development: About 80 hectares is proposed to be acquired at Hoskote for transport-related infrastructure
Why Corridor Matters
■ 80,000+ PCUs: Current traffic volume on NH-75
■ 1.5 lakh PCUs: Traffic could potentially reach this level in the coming years, according to those advocating additional road capacity
■ 17 km: Length of the proposed K R Pura-Hoskote Metro extension
■ 19%: Estimated EIRR cited in the feasibility report
(*Estimates, not official figures)
Earlier PlanMetro had earlier been proposed from Kadugodi: BMRCL had earlier considered extending Metro from Kadugodi, the Purple Line’s terminal station, to Hoskote via Whitefield-Hoskote Road. The corporation is constructing an elevated line of about 420 metres from Kadugodi station to facilitate train turnaround and improve operational efficiency.
Earlier, there were also plans to extend Metro from Kadugodi station, the terminal station of the Purple Line, to Hoskote via the Whitefield-Hoskote Road. BMRCL has taken up construction of an elevated line for about 420 metres from Kadugodi station to facilitate train turnaround and improve operational efficiency.

briefs.headline: Fake PAN card used in private firm officer’s name in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Police registered an FIR after a man complained that unknown persons had misused his personal details, photograph and documents to fraudulently create and use a PAN card.
Sayan Guha, 42, senior officer in a private firm, told police unknown persons misused his photograph, mobile number and other personal records/documents to fraudulently obtain and use the PAN card (no. DHFPS6843N). Sayan said his original PAN number is different.
He categorically told police he never applied for or use PAN card (DHFPS6843N) nor did he authorise any individual or entity to create or use it on his behalf.
The alleged misuse has left Sayan concerned that the disputed PAN card may have been used for financial, business, tax, banking or other transactions. He fears if such transactions were carried out using the disputed PAN, they could potentially result in financial liabilities, adverse records or other consequences being wrongly attributed to him.
The complaint points to an earlier business dispute that he feels may be relevant to the circumstances surrounding the identity misuse. Sayan stated that in 2016, he was involved in a business venture with two friends. Due to an alleged fraud, a case was filed by him in May 2017. Sayan claimed that in light of the earlier dispute, he has reasons to suspect the involvement of his earlier partner.
A case was registered under the Information Technology Act at Annapoorneshwarinagar police station.

briefs.headline: Karnataka SIR: More than 23,700 Form-7 applications received after claims and objections period
briefs.bodyText:
Even after the claims and objections period got over, at least 23,770 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names from electoral rolls were received between September 24, a day after the claims and objections period ended, and October 1, data from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, show.
This new revelation comes a day after Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and his Cabinet colleagues staged an over-five-hour protest at the Karnataka CEO’s office and made the CEO relent, ordering legal action over false claims in bulk Form-7 applications filed across the State. In Bhalki, Babaleshwar, Belagavi North, Kodagu and several other constituencies, pre-filled Form-7 applications were filed in bulk, mostly targeting Muslim voters.
The number of Form-7 applications received between June 16, when the electoral rolls were frozen ahead of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), and September 24 stood at 61,130. As of October 1, the number had increased to 84,990, a whopping rise of about 40%.
Applications filed after the claims and objections period will be considered only after the SIR process, while those filed up to September 23 will be considered for the final electoral rolls, scheduled to be published on October 27. In a press release on Friday, however, the CEO’s office said, “Out of the 84,900 Form-7 received, the number of forms received for objection to proposed inclusion is nil.”
District-wise data also show a significant increase in Form-7 applications after the claims and objections period ended. In Kodagu, for instance, the number increased from 696 applications received until September 23 to 1,143 as of October 1. In Shivamogga, the figure rose from 3,685 to 5,760 over the same period.
The Hindu had reported that bulk filing continued even after the objections period ended in constituencies such as Bhalki in Bidar district. The statutory Form-10 report shows that 1,131 applications were received in Bhalki between September 24 and 29, of which 1,123 were bulk filings.
When asked about the figures on applications, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar maintained that they were “as per the dashboard data”.
Meanwhile, of the 43,82,306 notices issued during the SIR, only 39,169 are yet to be delivered. Hearings have been completed in 35,60,833 cases, while more than 7.82 lakh hearings remain pending. The last hearing will be conducted on October 12, the CEO’s office said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka’s Innoverse aims to bridge the ‘third valley of death’ for deeptech start-ups
briefs.deck: The first cohort brings together start-ups working across five priority sectors, developing technologies spanning autonomous systems, indigenous navigation, regenerative medicine, orbital computing, counter-drone systems and solid propulsion
briefs.bodyText:
The prototype is ready, the technology works, the first clients have signed the deal. And yet, for a deeptech start-up, none of these may mean that the hardest part is over. They still need to cross what is known as the “third valley of death”, the stage where initial traction for a product needs to be scaled into sustained commercial growth.
Innoverse Foundation, a Section 8 entity under Karnataka’s IT-BT Department, intends to extend a hand to the start-ups that are crossing the third valley through its DeepTech Enabler programme, and has announced its first cohort of growth-stage start-ups.
The first cohort brings together start-ups working across five priority sectors, developing technologies spanning autonomous systems, indigenous navigation, regenerative medicine, orbital computing, counter-drone systems and solid propulsion.
The first cohort
The DeepTech Enabler programme is envisioned as an annual nine-month cohort of up to 10 start-ups. It is focused on start-ups that have proven product-market fit, sizeable revenue and a funding base, but require coordinated access to infrastructure, anchor customers, manufacturing readiness, regulatory support and scale-up capital.
AquaAirX Autonomous Systems, Fibroheal Woundcare, Hyspace Technologies Pvt Ltd (SkyServe), OptM Media Solutions, SpaceFields, UNMANND Autonomy, and Yaanendriya are the seven start-ups selected for the first cohort.
AquaAirX Autonomous Systems has been developing autonomous, amphibious and underwater systems for defence and maritime applications. Fibroheal Woundcare focuses on advanced biomaterial-based healthcare solutions using silk protein science for wound care, tissue regeneration, surgical applications and regenerative medicine.
Hyspace Technologies has been building onboard computing infrastructure that enables satellites to process data and generate actionable insights directly in orbit. OptM Media Solutions works on indigenous, edge-AI-enabled autonomous ground-vehicle systems and middleware for defence, while SpaceFields has been developing indigenous solid-propellant and allied technologies for space, aerospace and defence.
UNMANND Autonomy builds autonomous aerial systems, including high-altitude logistics drones and counter-drone systems, and Yaanendriya develops indigenous sensing, navigation and embedded control systems for defence, aerospace, robotics and industrial applications.
Crossing the bridge
“The first cohort of the Innoverse DeepTech Enabler represents the kind of technology capabilities that can have a significant impact across strategic sectors. By bringing together industry, infrastructure, capital, markets and policy support around these companies, we can create stronger pathways for Karnataka-born technologies to scale nationally and globally,” said IT-BT Minister Priyank Kharge.
The DeepTech Enabler will work with each start-up to create measurable progress across the defined problem statements through a company-specific engagement plan.
“The seven companies in our first cohort have already demonstrated that they can build and validate difficult technologies. The challenge now is different. They need the right customers, infrastructure, regulatory pathways, capital and ecosystem partnerships to move from individual deployments to repeatable commercial scale,” said Pravin Hungund, CEO, Innoverse Foundation.
“The role of Innoverse is to bring these pieces together around each company and build a pathway that is specific to its growth requirements. We want Cohort 1 to demonstrate that deeptech companies can be systematically supported to cross the Third Valley of Death,” he added.
Specific targets
Alongside the Enabler, Innoverse is also developing the Innoverse Connect Programme, which will provide targeted support to early revenue-generating start-ups facing specific challenges.
Innoverse has set specific growth ambitions for the first cohorts of the Enabler and Connect programmes, targeting a twofold increase in the combined annual revenue of the cohort from approximately ₹35 crore to ₹70 crore. It also aims to mobilise growth capital from approximately ₹150 crore to more than ₹300 crore.
Cohort 1 will run through June 2027, with progress tracked against its revenue and capital targets as well as the anchor-customer contracts, certifications and international market-entry pathways secured for each company. Applications for Cohort 2 are expected to open after the completion of the first cohort.

briefs.headline: Eleven, including a couple, held in assault case in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru police have arrested 11 persons, including a couple, in connection with an alleged attempt to kill a man over an old enmity in southwest Bengaluru’s Subramanyapura.
The accused have been identified as Manikanta, 27; his wife, Keerthana, 21; Prem V.; Manoj G.; Krishnagupta; Akash, alias Mandya; Munna; Madhusudhan; Darshan S.; Sudeep M.N.; and Bharath M.G., all in their 20s.
The accused allegedly attempted to murder the complainant over an old enmity related to a cricket match played two months ago. They attacked two persons in separate incidents using daggers, long weapons, and iron rods.
The first incident occurred on September 20 at a vacant site in Uttarahalli. The complainant and his friends were standing there when around six to seven persons arrived on motorcycles and attacked the complainant and his friend with daggers.
In another incident on the same day, the complainant was having food near Uttarahalli Main Road when more than five persons allegedly arrived on motorcycles and attacked him with iron rods. The accused reportedly also assaulted the complainant’s nephew, who intervened.
Two cases were registered at the Subramanyapura police station on September 21. Using technical evidence, the police questioned Keerthana about the whereabouts of the accused, but she provided wrong information, concealing the fact that the accused had visited her place, police sources said.
“We reviewed CCTV footage in the vicinity and found that the accused had visited her house. Subsequently, we questioned her again, which gave leads about the whereabouts of the accused,” an investigator in the case said.
According to the officer, the accused and the victim had played a cricket match about two months ago, during which they had fought over bats and wickets. To take revenge, the accused allegedly planned the attack.
All the accused were produced before a court and taken into police custody for further interrogation. Four accused, including the woman, have since been remanded in judicial custody, while interrogation of the remaining seven is under way, the police said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper service likely to start this month, to operate six days a week
briefs.deck: The service, numbered 27652 from KSR Bengaluru to CSMT and 27651 in the return direction, has been approved based on the minutes of a meeting held on February 16, 2026, as per the Railway Board communication accessed by The Hindu
briefs.bodyText:
The Railway Board has approved the introduction of a Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between KSR Bengaluru and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai, and is likely to start operations from this month, according to officials.
The service, numbered 27652 from KSR Bengaluru to CSMT and 27651 in the return direction, has been approved based on the minutes of a meeting held on February 16, 2026, as per the Railway Board communication accessed by The Hindu.
As per the proposed schedule, Train 27652 will depart KSR Bengaluru at 10 p.m. and reach Dharmavaram at 12.50 a.m., Wadi at 5.05 a.m. and CSMT at 1.50 p.m. the following day.
In the return direction, Train 27651 will depart CSMT at 10.30 p.m., reach Wadi at 7.25 a.m., Dharmavaram at 11.45 a.m. and arrive at KSR Bengaluru at 2.50 p.m. The train will have stoppages at Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan, in addition to its originating and terminating stations.
The service is proposed to operate six days a week. The Bengaluru-Mumbai service will operate except on Mondays, while the Mumbai-Bengaluru service will operate except on Tuesdays.
The Railway Board document states that the service will use two Vande Bharat Sleeper trainsets. Solapur and Pune have been identified for watering and other associated terminal-related arrangements.
The board has also directed the railway zones concerned to take necessary action for introducing the service at an early convenient date. It has suggested that, if required, the inaugural train could initially be operated as a special service and subsequently integrated into the regular timetable.
The proposed sleeper service would provide an overnight rail connection between Bengaluru and Mumbai, with the journey covering major cities and railway hubs across Karnataka and Maharashtra. Earlier, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had indicated that the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper service was expected to be introduced soon and this would be the first Vande Bharat Sleeper for South India.
Sleeper train
Nearly six years after India introduced its first Vande Bharat Express in 2019, the country’s first commercial Vande Bharat Sleeper service began operations on January 22, 2026. Operated by the Northeast Frontier Railway, the inaugural service runs between Kamakhya in Guwahati and Howrah, covering around 972 km in approximately 14 hours.
Designed primarily for overnight journeys on routes ranging between 800 km and 1,200 km, the Vande Bharat Sleeper is intended to offer faster travel and improved passenger comfort on long-distance routes. The new service is also expected to gradually serve as an alternative to conventional premium overnight trains, including the Rajdhani Express, on select corridors.
A 16-coach Vande Bharat Sleeper train comprises 11 Third AC (3AC) coaches, four Second AC (2AC) coaches and one First AC (1AC) coach, providing accommodation for 823 passengers. The train has 611 berths in 3AC, 188 in 2AC and 24 in 1AC.
The fully air-conditioned train incorporates a range of modern amenities aimed at enhancing passenger convenience and safety. These include automatic sliding doors, CCTV surveillance, bio-vacuum toilets, sensor-based water taps, individual reading lights, mobile charging points and digital passenger information displays. Onboard catering is also available, with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian meal options.
For enhanced safety, the train is equipped with the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system, along with emergency talk-back facilities. The driver cabins are fully air-conditioned and feature dedicated washrooms.

stories.headline: Sea of red for most asset classes
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Nine months into 2026, most asset classes in the domestic market are signalling red in their respective year-to-date return columns.
Data shows that so far this year, while sensex has given a negative return of 16%, Nifty has returned 15% in the red. In the bond segment also, with yields rising, investors have seen negative returns in their portfolio.
Internationally, gold and silver prices have given negative returns. Although the rupee has weakened 7% so far in the year, domestic returns are in low single digits in gold and negative in silver.
Only investors in crude oil have made good money—thanks mainly to the US-Iran war in the Persian Gulf that has led to a 67% gain in Brent crude. Outside of the popular assets, copper has given a smart return. The red metal has jumped from the $5.6/ounce level at the start of the year to the $6.5 level now, a 15% return. Looking ahead, inflationary expectations due to rising crude oil prices and, along with them, a weak rupee, could spook investors.
A recent report by SBI Mutual Fund warned that inflation was a unifying macro theme of the year. For one, a delayed monsoon and lingering weather effects have depressed sowing activity and lifted food price risks, posing near-term challenges for rural incomes, the report said.
The fund house also pointed out that input costs—from power and fuel in cement, to needle coke in electrodes, to milk procurement, freight, labour and packaging—are broadening rather than easing.
“These pressures are already driving selective price hikes across FMCG, food diagnostics, consumer staples and several industrial categories. The ability to pass on these costs varies widely by sector. Fertilisers, agrochemicals and speciality chemicals face the most severe cost mismatches, with fertiliser economics particularly dependent on additional subsidy support as subsidy rates have not kept pace with raw material inflation. The world is in an inflationary boom, not yet an inflationary bust. A further rise in oil, or high bond yields starting to hurt growth, could tip it into a bust,” the report said.
On the equities front, the fund house’s asset allocation framework continues to favour a 60:40 equity–fixed income allocation (versus a 50:50 benchmark). “It projects an early-teens equity CAGR at the large-cap index level over three years. Historically, a low level of market polarisation supports a tilt towards large caps.” On the debt side, the report said that the shorter end of the yield curve is offering relatively attractive opportunities, meaning investments in short-term papers are better bets than medium- or long-term ones.
In the short run, RBI policy decision will be the key domestic trigger, with pressure to support the rupee and contain imported inflation strengthening expectations of a rate hike, said Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments. “With corporate earnings for Q2 expected to be softer than Q1, sentiment is likely to remain fragile. A meaningful de-escalation in West Asia could trigger a sharp relief rally. Until then, investors should stay selective, favouring earnings visibility.”

stories.headline: What is happening to the Indian IT bench? | Explained
stories.deck: Once a strategic buffer against fluctuating project demand, the IT bench is becoming a more tightly managed pool of talent, shaped by utilisation, changing demand and the growing premium on specialised skills
stories.bodyText:
The story so far: Wipro recently changed how long some of its employees can remain without a billable project. Under its revised bench policy, effective October 1, employees in Band 2 and below can reportedly remain unallocated for up to 180 calendar days. For Band 3 and above, the standard period is 45 days, while employees with disabilities have a 75-day period. Employees in Band 2 and below who remain unallocated for 180 days can be separated under their employment contracts. Wipro did not respond to queries from The Hindu.
The change comes as recent industry estimates point to shorter bench periods and lower bench strength. Average bench time at large IT-services companies was estimated at 35–45 days in 2025, compared with 45–60 days in FY20 and FY21. The proportion of employees on the bench was estimated at 2–5%, down from 10–15% earlier.
So what exactly is the bench, and why has it been such an important part of the Indian IT business model?
What is the bench?
In IT services, the bench is broadly the pool of employees on a company’s payroll who are not currently assigned to a billable client project. They may be waiting for another assignment, undergoing training or working on internal initiatives. The exact definition can vary between companies.
The bench exists because companies have to balance workforce capacity against uneven project demand. A company that wins a large project needs people ready to work on it, but hiring, training and demand do not always happen at the same time. Carrying some spare capacity allows faster deployment when demand materialises, but a company continues to incur employee costs while those employees are not generating billable revenue.
That is why utilisation matters. A higher proportion of employees who are not deployed on billable work can weigh on utilisation and margins. But being on the bench does not necessarily mean being unproductive. It could mean employees may be training, working on internal projects or developing skills for another deployment.
When did the bench become part of Indian IT?
There is little evidence of a single point at which the Indian IT industry introduced a formal bench model. Company records show that unallocated capacity was already being measured and discussed by the early 2000s.
In April 2001, Infosys told analysts that the company had “slightly more than 1,000 people on the bench” at the end of the quarter. Utilisation excluding training was 73%; the remaining unbilled effort included employees on the bench as well as those on leave, management, research and development and internal information-systems projects.
Such disclosures show that unallocated capacity was already an identifiable part of workforce management at a major Indian IT-services company by the early 2000s.
Why did companies carry a bench?
A large bench was not always regarded as waste. When companies expected demand to rise, retaining trained employees allowed them to respond to new projects without having to recruit and train an entirely new workforce.
Wipro’s FY2011-12 annual report points to its investment in a “strategic bench to fuel growth”, which contributed to gross utilisation falling from 69.9% in FY11 to 68.3% in FY12.
The bench could therefore be both an investment and a cost, where companies could deliberately carry employees ahead of expected demand, accepting lower utilisation in anticipation of future projects.
Why did just-in-time hiring emerge?
The economics of carrying a bench changed when demand weakened. Spare capacity that could be deployed quickly during a growth phase became a cost when projects were delayed or failed to materialise.
Wipro’s October 2009 earnings call illustrates the shift. Then CEO Suresh Vaswani said the company’s bench had fallen from around 11,000 employees to about 7,000 and that Wipro had made its “people supply chain” tighter and more “just-in-time” in hiring and recruitment.
HCL Technologies took a similar approach during the 2008-09 downturn. Then CEO Vineet Nayar said the company had adopted “just in time hiring”, arguing that people could be hired at seven days’ notice and that there was therefore “no point of increasing your bench.”
The history is therefore not a simple journey from large benches to small ones. Companies have moved between carrying spare capacity and tightly controlling it depending on demand and utilisation.
How did companies make the bench productive?
Some companies tried to change what happened to employees between projects rather than simply reduce their numbers.
Persistent Systems said in its FY2016-17 annual report that the need to leverage employees when they were not working on customer projects had led to the “dissolution of the Bench” and the creation of TeXT, or Transforming Employee Experiences. Employees between projects could work on timed projects involving AI, machine learning, natural language processing, IoT and analytics.
Infosys launched its Zero Bench programme in 2015, creating an internal marketplace for employees awaiting longer-term assignments. In its FY2015-16 annual report, Infosys said the programme was intended to “eradicate the bench”. Within nine months, more than 12,000 jobs had been created on the marketplace, and more than 67% of employees who were on the bench had completed at least one assignment.
Eliminating the bench as an idle period is not necessarily the same as eliminating employees being between client projects. The interval can instead be filled with internal work, training or other assignments.
What is AI changing?
AI is changing what makes an employee deployable. IT-services companies are increasingly linking workforce planning to skills and reskilling. TCS’s FY2025-26 annual report says its talent model is centred on skills, roles and talent, and reports more than 2.7 lakh employees with advanced AI and machine-learning proficiency.
Wipro’s FY2025-26 filing describes a “Skill as a Currency” approach involving upskilling, reskilling and cross-skilling, while Infosys’s FY2025-26 ESG report says its AI strategy includes enabling employees to be deployed to relevant projects through upskilling.
The bench is therefore increasingly a skills-matching problem as well as a headcount problem. An employee can be available but not immediately deployable if their skills do not match the projects entering the pipeline.
Therefore, AI is not simply shrinking the bench. It is changing the definition of who is deployable.
Who bears the risk?
A bench is a buffer against uncertain demand, but it involves a trade-off for companies. Maintaining one means carrying the cost of employees without billable assignments, while maintaining too little means risking a shortage of trained talent when demand picks up.
For employees, a shorter bench window leaves less time to find another assignment, and prolonged non-deployment can eventually put the employee’s job at risk. Skills mismatch can add to that risk, as an employee may be available but not suitable for the projects in the pipeline.
Therefore, the bench becomes a balancing act for both sides, with companies managing capacity and employees managing deployment risk.

stories.headline: Pay the Global South for climate damage, but only if it prices carbon, says economist Greenstone
stories.deck: Michael Greenstone, Director of the Energy Policy Institute of the University of Chicago, says that the exact parameters of agreements would have to be negotiated
stories.bodyText:
Rich countries should pay people in developing countries for the climate damage their emissions cause, on condition that those countries put a price on carbon. That is the central proposal of a forthcoming book, Just Economics, by University of Chicago economist Michael Greenstone, with Nobel-Prize winning economists Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo.
“We’re proposing Indians receive money unencumbered,” Mr. Greenstone, who is Director, Energy Policy Institute, University of Chicago, said in an interview. “Spend it on whatever you want. That is based on the amount of damage the OECD countries’ emissions are doing.” The payment, he said, “would go directly to the people, not to the government.”
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), is a grouping of mostly wealthy, industrialised countries that has contributed to most of the accumulated carbon in the atmosphere driving global warming. This contrasts with the “Global South”, meaning low- and middle-income countries but whose emissions are fast rising.
“82% of the emissions going forward are projected to be outside the OECD and moral appeals have failed,” he reckoned, “the better angels-argument ain’t working.” However the transfer would be “contingent on the Global South adopting carbon pricing. It’s not for free. It’s a deal. You have to give something to get something.”
Mr. Greenstone said it was possible to calculate the damage from carbon emissions to India. “However the exact parameters of that will have to be negotiated. Such a deal did not require the whole world and could be struck between, say, the European Union and India, he argued.
He pointed to “the more or less complete failure of climate finance to the Global South” and said “it’s time to think about a new approach.” Next month countries are expected to convene in Turkey for the annual climate meet.
Market-based solutions
Much of Mr. Greenstone’s work is around designing market-based solutions to address pollution. Most prominent is the Surat Emissions Trading Scheme for controlling particulate matter, first mooted with the Gujarat Pollution Control Board in 2010. In a randomised trial, 150 textile plants were assigned to a market and 150 stayed under conventional regulation. Compliance in the market was “99%”, against about a third of industries out of compliance at any time under the status quo. This happened because researchers could see what firms bid to buy and sell pollution permits: “The price I want for that has got to be at least what it cost me to do it. From those bids, we were able to infer how expensive it was to achieve different levels of total emissions. Cutting emissions proved cheap, because the guys had all the equipment and just had to start operating it or maintaining it,” he explained. Enforcement mattered. When firms fell short of permits, the regulator levied a fine of ten times the permit value. “Once the industry saw that the rules were going to be enforced then everything changed,” he said.
While the Surat system was designed to reduce particulate matter from textile mills, the next stop is Maharashtra, where the market will cover sulphur dioxide — a gaseous pollutant — and include large power plants. He said that a “mock trading period involving an actual market, without real money, was under way to get firms used to trading permits before the real market opened.
Similar conversations are on with Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Haryana. Gujarat’s Pollution Control Board has itself asked for help designing a water market and a Statewide sulphur dioxide market. If States get their own markets working, he said, “one could imagine linking those markets”.
The challenge that enforcement agencies faced is the inability to track a plant’s emissions second by second. Industries, for competitive advantage, frequently resorted to turning off pollution monitoring equipment. “ This is the Achilles heel of environmental regulation around the world.” Finding the upper limit to the pollutants that industries could be permitted to emit is the other big challenge. “It is a judgement about the right trade-off between economic costs and environmental quality.”

stories.headline: ‘Workers growing increasingly anxious’: US adds 29k jobs, far below 90k expected
stories.deck: US employers added only 29,000 jobs in September, significantly lower than economists' expectations of 90,000. The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% as more people entered the workforce without immediate jobs. Healthcare hiring showed a notable slowdown, with government job cuts further contributing to weak hiring figures. While layoffs decreased by 18%, hiring plans fell sharply, reaching their…
stories.bodyText:
US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, well below expectations, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, according to government data released on Friday, pointing to a slowdown in hiring as the US heads towards pivotal midterm elections.
Hiring fell sharply from a revised 133,000 in August, the labour department said. Economists had expected employers to add around 90,000 jobs last month.
Revisions to earlier data also reduced combined July and August payrolls by 60,000 jobs.
The unemployment rate increased from 4.1% in August to 4.2%. The rise came partly as 485,000 people entered the workforce in September, with not all of them finding jobs immediately.
Average hourly wages rose 3% from a year earlier, marking the smallest year-over-year increase since May 2021.
Healthcare hiring slows as governments cut jobs
The September figures showed weaker hiring across several parts of the economy. Federal, state and local governments cut 17,000 jobs, while professional and business services companies reduced payrolls by 9,000.
Healthcare companies added 17,000 jobs, but that was around half their average monthly gain of 33,000 over the past year.
Bradley Saunders, an economist at Capital Economics, was quoted by news agency AP as saying the slowdown in healthcare hiring might reflect the Trump administration's revocation of work authorisations for 350,000 Haitians.
Construction companies added 11,000 jobs, while manufacturers increased payrolls by 9,000.
The latest report comes after jobless claims remained low. Initial applications for unemployment benefits fell to 197,000 in the week ending September 26, the lowest level since mid-July.
The four-week average fell to 200,000.
Planned layoffs by US-based employers fell 18% in September to 43,281, while announced job cuts were down 20% from a year earlier.
However, employers' hiring plans were down 23% year-on-year and September's total was the lowest for the month since 2011.
Jobs data puts focus back on Federal Reserve
The weaker hiring figures could draw greater attention from the Federal Reserve to its mandate of maximum employment. Several Fed officials had recently said inflation remained their primary focus.
The US central bank has been dealing with inflation that has remained above its 2% target for more than five years.
The latest employment figures could affect the debate over whether to keep interest rates unchanged at the Fed's next meeting rather than raise them.
The labour market has remained relatively resilient despite trade tensions, persistent inflation, high interest rates and the conflict with Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher.
At the same time, indicators of worker confidence have weakened. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index fell to its lowest level in more than a decade, with more than 28% of respondents expecting fewer jobs to be available in six months, compared with 14% who expected more.
Glassdoor's employee confidence index also fell last month to its lowest level since records began in 2016. It was the third record low for the index this year.
“Employee confidence has been continuously grinding downward over the last year as workers grow increasingly anxious about everything from layoffs to AI,” Glassdoor chief economist Daniel Zhao said, as cited by AP.
Low hiring, low layoffs define job market
The latest data reflect a labour market in which employers are not cutting large numbers of existing workers but are also adding relatively few new employees.
The labour department's measure of gross hiring has remained subdued for more than two years.
Glassdoor's Zhao said workers were increasingly reluctant to leave their existing jobs because finding new employment could take longer.
“They often feel stuck,” Zhao said. “Workers aren’t finding there’s opportunity on the open market to find a better job – one that pays more or offers better work-life balance.”
The average unemployed person had been out of work for more than six months in August, the longest average period of joblessness since February 2022.
The September jobs report is the last major employment report before the November 3 US midterm elections, when voters will decide whether President Donald Trump's Republicans retain full control of Congress.
Financial markets initially reacted positively to the jobs data. Futures for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite added to their gains, while the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 5.17% from 5.24% a day earlier.

briefs.headline: UPI volume jumps 27% to touch 145 bn in first half

briefs.bodyText:

Industry watchers attributed the dip to the fact August has 31 days versus 30 in September and pointed out average transactions/day were higher in September at 802 million versus 791 million in August. NPCI, an initiative of the RBI and the Indian Banks’ Association, is an umbrella organisation for retail payments and settlement systems in India. It runs UPI used for real-time payments between peers or at merchants’ end while making purchases.
