briefs.headline: GOBARdhan eyes 10-fold increase in CBG output: Hardeep Singh Puri
briefs.deck: Hardeep Singh Puri said the scheme provides capital assistance as well as guaranteed offtake of the renewable fuel made by processing organic waste such as agricultural residue, animal dung, food waste and other biomass
briefs.bodyText:
The ₹23,731-crore GOBARdhan scheme aims to drive a 10-fold increase in compressed biogas (CBG) production, save more than ₹40,000 crore in fuel imports, add over ₹75,000 crore to GDP and create more than 1.5 lakh jobs, as the government seeks to turn agricultural and organic waste into a new source of domestic energy.
Speaking at the formal launch of the scheme, Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said the scheme provides capital assistance as well as guaranteed offtake of the renewable fuel made by processing organic waste such as agricultural residue, animal dung, food waste and other biomass.
Capital support plus guaranteed offtake is likely to lift CBG (essentially methane-rich gas) from current 0.4 million standard cubic metre per day to 4-6 mmscmd, he said, hoping this would help in achieving the target of raising share of natural gas — a cleaner-burning, lower-pollution fuel — in energy basket to 15% by 2030 from the current 6-7%.
Replace fossil fuel
The scheme is designed to replace about 10 million tonne of fossil fuel with clean gas, potentially cutting more than 40 million tonne of CO2 emissions, while producing around 250 million tonne of organic manure for farmers. Mr. Puri said the programme would help turn farmers from “Annadatas to also being the Urjadatas”.
The scheme provides capital assistance of up to ₹30 crore per CBG project across the two eligible capital-support components. For greenfield plants, assistance is set at ₹1.25 crore per tonne per day (TPD) of eligible CBG capacity. Brownfield projects can receive support at 50% of the applicable greenfield rate for additional capacity created through fresh investment.
Plant upgrades
Existing biogas plants upgraded to make CBG can get ₹0.60 crore/TPD, subject to a ₹5-crore project ceiling. To make CBG projects commercially viable, the Centre is offering producers assured offtake of up to 100% eligible output at an administered price of ₹2,110 per million British thermal units - equivalent to about ₹98/ kg.

briefs.headline: Auto-component order wins: Decoding LTV and its implications for revenue visibility
briefs.deck: LTV measures the size of the opportunity, not the speed at which it reaches the revenue line. It needs to be read alongside duration, SOP and revenue ramp-up.
briefs.bodyText:
When an auto-component maker announces a ₹2,000-crore order win, investors want to know how much will translate into revenue — and when.
The answer is not always evident from the headline number. Component suppliers often win contracts for a vehicle platform’s life, with volumes ramping up, peaking and then tapering. This is why some companies use lifetime value (LTV) rather than annualised order value.
LTV is the estimated total sales a supplier expects from a vehicle programme over its production life.
Rane (Madras), for instance, shifted from annualised business wins to LTV in the June quarter. In its Q1 FY27 earnings call, the company said it had benchmarked the practice against Indian and global peers and that most programmes run for more than six years. It reported ₹2,040 crore of new business on an LTV basis.
A Rane official told The Hindu that LTV is derived from the expected programme life and estimated OEM volumes when the order is secured. Dividing LTV by programme duration, it said, would not yield a meaningful annual figure because volumes vary over the programme.
Global suppliers use the metric too. Autoliv said in its 2025 annual report that delivery contracts typically cover a vehicle model’s life, generally five to seven years. Its LTV estimates factor in prices and production volumes, while the typical lead time from order intake to start of production is one to three years.
For investors, LTV provides visibility on the long-term business pipeline. But it does not answer the immediate question: when does the revenue arrive?
Consider two programmes: one with an LTV of ₹1,000 crore over 10 years and another of ₹700 crore over three years. The first has the larger LTV, but the second could generate revenue faster.
A Chennai-based chartered accountant with more than 15 years of practice, who reviewed the issue for The Hindu, said LTV indicates the size of a long-term programme but does not provide sufficient near-term revenue visibility by itself.
Investors should ideally see LTV alongside programme duration, start of production (SOP), annualised or peak value and revenue ramp-up, the CA said. Customer-volume assumptions and other conditions also matter.
Can LTV be divided by years?
Rane’s ₹2,040-crore LTV divided by six years gives ₹340 crore a year. But that is only an average, not a revenue forecast. Volumes can be lower during ramp-up, peak in the middle and decline thereafter.
Pratik Kothari of Unique PMS, who raised the issue during Rane’s earnings call, noted that the company had earlier disclosed peak order value and programme duration separately. Investors can still “divide by 6 and get annual/peak value”, he said.
Mr. Kothari does not see the change as an attempt to inflate order wins. “There is no perception building,” he said, adding that there was “nothing sensational about it”.
Rane official said meaningful revenue from orders typically begins 12–24 months after the award, with the full contribution generally coming over the following three to six years, sometimes longer. The company does not provide year-by-year guidance on commercially sensitive parameters because SOPs, ramp-ups and customer platform decisions can change.
No industry-wide template
There is no industry-wide disclosure practice. Some suppliers report LTV, others annual or peak value, while some provide neither.
Suprajit Engineering, for example, has disclosed both, reporting in June 2026 new contracts worth about $12 million annually, with an estimated LTV of $75 million.

briefs.headline: Gold's Rs 1.5 lakh price drives buyers to silver who get 650g silver at same price
briefs.deck: At current prices, 10 grams of 24-karat gold costs around Rs 1.5 lakh, an amount that would buy approximately 650 grams of silver. With gold prices remaining prohibitively high for a large section of middle-class buyers, the white metal is steadily attracting attention. High gold prices have made the precious metal out of reach for several people.
briefs.bodyText:
This festive season, Indians may opt to buy silver instead of gold as prices of the yellow metal stay high despite the recent fall. Silver, traditionally playing a supporting role to gold in India's jewellery market, is now poised for a much bigger moment.
With gold prices remaining prohibitively high for a large section of middle-class buyers, the white metal is steadily attracting attention. High gold prices have made the precious metal out of reach for several people.
Betting on silver instead of gold
Jewellers and traders are expanding their offerings, ranging from ornaments and idols to furniture, to draw both consumers and investors. Silver, once largely overshadowed by gold, is emerging as a possible standout this festive season, which begins with Navratri on October 11.
Several jewellers and an industry expert told ET that silver is expected to make up a greater proportion of jewellery purchases during the festival period.
Why silver is gaining ground this festive season
- Affordability for middle-class buyers: At approximately Rs 2.3 lakh per kg, silver provides a much cheaper starting point than gold.
- Investment appeal among affluent consumers: Some buyers are anticipating further appreciation, with hopes that prices could climb back to Rs 4 lakh per kg.
- Growing contribution to jewellers' earnings: One jeweller says silver now generates 25-30% of total revenue, compared with 10% two years ago.
“I am a third-generation diamond jeweller based in Surat. But today, I earn more from silver than from diamonds,” said Nagnesh Pachchigar of SN Jewellers. Silver contributes up to 35% of his yearly revenue.

Unscrupulous jewellers may use fake stamps to mark your gold: As hallmarking charges rise to Rs 75 from Rs 45 Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council flags risk of rise in fraudsters
At current prices, 10 grams of 24-karat gold costs around Rs 1.5 lakh, an amount that would buy approximately 650 grams of silver.
Pachchigar is placing his biggest bets on silver this festive season, reflecting a clear change in what consumers are choosing to buy. He said middle-class households are increasingly opting for silver articles as gifts because they are more affordable.
“Silver is clearly the next gold. I expect 40% of our annual silver sales only during the monthlong festive season starting with Navratri,” Pachchigar said.
Surendra Mehta, national secretary of the India Bullion and Jewellers Association, said, “We estimate that silver buying during this Diwali season will rise by 17- 18% from the corresponding period last year.”
According to Mehta, availability is no longer a hurdle for the market. In July, the government relaxed restrictions on silver imports that had been imposed in May, partly as a measure to limit foreign exchange outflows. Imports responded sharply, crossing $1 billion in August, a 127% increase from the same month a year earlier, commerce ministry data showed.
Gold hallmarking rates rise
Meanwhile, gold hallmarking, which enables buyers to check the purity of the metal they are purchasing, now comes at a higher cost. The increase has also triggered fears that counterfeit stamps could become more common, with fraudsters passing off fake hallmarks as genuine.
The industry is concerned that the higher fee may prompt dishonest jewellers to use forged hallmarking marks to avoid the additional expense.
This risk is being viewed as particularly significant in tier-2, tier-3 and tier-4 cities, where awareness among consumers is still relatively low.
Although buyers ultimately bear the hallmarking charge when they purchase jewellery, many do not know that the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number can be checked using the Bureau of Indian Standards' Care mobile application.
The GJC has approached consumer affairs minister Pralhad Joshi and the BIS, seeking a rollback of the fee to its earlier level of Rs 45 per article from the current Rs 75.
The charge applicable to silver jewellery remains unchanged at Rs 35 per article.
The new charges were formally announced under the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, notified on September 14, 2026.

briefs.headline: Sebi penalises SMC Global Securities for compliance lapses
briefs.deck: The market watchdog found that SMC Global Securities had not maintained appropriate pre-order placement records for certain clients and could not provide relevant records for multiple orders, Sebi said
briefs.bodyText:
Capital market regulator Sebi has levied a ₹1 lakh fine on city-based SMC Global Securities for failing to comply with norms on maintaining client order-placement records and supervision of an authorised person.
The order came after the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) conducted a thematic inspection of the stock broker for the period January-September 2024, focusing on unauthorised trading complaints and client order placement.
The market watchdog found that SMC Global Securities had not maintained appropriate pre-order placement records for certain clients and could not provide relevant records for multiple orders, Sebi said in an order passed on Thursday (October 1, 2026)
Sebi also found deficiencies in the broker's supervision of authorised person Amit Lilhare, including failure to adequately monitor bank accounts receiving commissions and verify payout requests from clients.
The order said that 161 of 343 active clients mapped to Lilhare showed a pattern of fixed payouts, involving client investments of ₹6.11 crore and payouts of over ₹1.84 crore during the inspection period.
Accordingly, SMC Global Securities flouted the Stock Brokers Regulations and other market norms.
SMC Global Securities is a Sebi-registered stock broker and a member of exchanges such as BSE, NSE, MCX and NCDEX.

stories.headline: Neeru Dhanda to be flag bearer at Asian Games closing
stories.deck: Neeru earned three medals at Nagoya: women’s individual trap gold, women’s team silver with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat, and trap mixed team gold with Chenai
stories.bodyText:
Ace Indian trap shooter Neeru Dhanda will be the women’s flag bearer at the closing ceremony of the Asian Games on Sunday (October 4, 2026) after capping a remarkable campaign with two gold medals and a team silver to emerge as one of the most successful athletes at the continental showpiece.
The 27-year-old, who returned to India a day after winning her third medal — a gold in the trap mixed team event alongside Kynan Chenai — will travel back to Nagoya on Saturday morning (October 3, 2026) to lead the Indian contingent at the closing ceremony.
“She is returning to Nagoya tomorrow morning to be the woman flag bearer. The decision on the male flag bearer will be taken tomorrow,” deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat said on Friday (October 2, 2026).
Bhagwat was present at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium to watch the women’s hockey final between India and China.
Neeru enjoyed a stellar campaign in Nagoya, winning the women’s individual trap gold before combining with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to clinch silver in the women’s team event.
She then partnered Chenai to win the trap mixed team gold on the penultimate day of the shooting competition, taking her medal tally to three.
Her two gold medals and a silver made her one of India’s standout performers at the Games, capping a historic campaign for the shooter, who had also won the women’s trap gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato earlier this year.

stories.headline: Kumkum Mohod wins Asian Games gold, secures India’s 2028 Olympic quota
stories.deck: Kumkum Mohod carved her name in history by clinching the gold medal in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games. Triumphing in a nail-biting shoot-out against South Korea’s Oh Yejin after a tied score, she also ensured India's presence at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics by securing a semifinal spot.
stories.bodyText:
Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a shoot-out here on Saturday.
With the victory, 
Kumkum
 became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event.
Asian Games Full Coverage
 | 
Schedule
 | 
Medal Tally
After the scores were tied at 5-5, Kumkum held her nerve in the shoot-out, shooting a 10 while Oh managed an 8 to hand the Indian the gold medal.
The victory capped a remarkable campaign for Kumkum, who had already secured an Olympic quota place for India by reaching the semifinals. She defeated China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2 to book her place in the final and assure herself of at least a silver medal.
Kumkum secured one of the two available quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. As per the rules, the quota belongs to the country.
Against Zhu, Kumkum won the opening set 28-27 after shooting 9, 10 and 9. The second set was shared after both archers shot three 10s, while the third set was also tied, leaving Kumkum with a 4-2 lead.
She then edged Zhu by a point in the final set to seal a 6-2 victory, with the scores reading 28-27, 30-30, 29-29 and 29-28.
Earlier in the day, Kumkum defeated reigning world champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4 in the quarterfinal.
The individual gold was her third medal at the Asian Games. Kumkum had earlier won the women’s team recurve gold alongside Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma, before combining with Dhiraj Bommadevara to claim mixed pair silver on Friday.
Kumkum’s gold also marked a landmark moment for Indian recurve archery, making her the first Indian woman to win a medal in the individual event at the Asian Games.

briefs.headline: Asian Games silver medallist Sreeshankar targets gold in 2028
briefs.deck: Sreeshankar won the silver medal in long jump at the Asian Games in Japan despite suffering an injury during his fourth attempt
briefs.bodyText:
Asian Games silver medallist long jumper M. Sreeshankar on Friday (October 2, 2026) expressed confidence that his fourth career silver medal would eventually pave the way for a major gold, saying he hoped to achieve the feat in 2028.
Mr. Sreeshankar won the silver medal at the Asian Games 2026 in Japan despite suffering an injury during his fourth attempt.
Speaking to reporters at his residence after returning from Japan, Mr. Sreeshankar said his physical condition and preparation were good enough for an 8.20 m-plus jump, but a slip while attempting the distance affected his performance.
“My body condition was good. I had all the conditions required to jump 8.20 m-plus. So, during the jump aimed at reaching 8.20 m, my leg went a bit forward, and I suddenly slipped and fell like Superman,” he said.
Narrow margins
Mr. Sreeshankar said he had missed gold by very narrow margins on previous occasions but believed those experiences were leading him towards a major triumph.
“If I get a gold in 2028, then everything will be compensated, for sure,” he said.
Asked whether winning the medal was a stroke of luck, Mr. Sreeshankar said the difficult weather conditions had made the competition unpredictable. “Definitely. Because in these weather conditions, the performance could go either way. It was raining heavily, but alongside the rain, it was also humid. So, jumping above 8 metres gave me good confidence,” he said.
He said he had expected jumps in the range of 8.10 m or 8.15 m but felt his 8.07 m effort was satisfactory under the circumstances.
The heat, humidity and rain had caused cramps among several athletes, making the ability to adapt to the conditions crucial to winning a medal, he said. “In these major competitions, whoever can overcome and adapt to that particular situation gets the medal,” he said.
Mr. Sreeshankar noted that all five athletes in the competition had previously recorded jumps of around 8.30 m or 8.40 m, making it a closely contested event.
He said the athletes finishing behind him had recorded jumps of 8.05 m and 8.06 m, with the second, third and fourth positions separated by just one centimetre.
To avoid aggravating injury
Mr. Sreeshankar said his muscles began cramping from his third attempt, forcing him to approach the jump cautiously to avoid aggravating the injury.
“I only had the intention of just completing that jump. If I applied too much force, those cramped muscles might have led to further injury. So, I had to take that attempt very easily,” he said.
Palakkad MP V.K. Sreekandan and Palakkad MLA Ramesh Pisharody also visited Mr. Sreeshankar’s residence to congratulate him on his feat.

briefs.headline: ‘A third peak’: De Villiers on Kohli’s aggressive ODI approach ahead of 2027 WC
briefs.deck: AB de Villiers shared his excitement over Virat Kohli's stellar performance in the ODIs against the West Indies, where Kohli's unbeaten 139 runs were pivotal for India's triumph. De Villiers highlighted the shift in Kohli's mindset, noting his newfound aggressiveness and positive outlook. He views this stage of Kohli's career as a remarkable resurgence, appreciating the strategic evolution he has…
briefs.bodyText:
AB de Villiers
 is delighted to see his old friend and Royal Challengers Bengaluru teammate 
Virat Kohli
 flourish in ODIs, the only format in which he now plays for India.
In the opening ODI against West Indies at Thiruvananthapuram, 
Kohli
 smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, hitting nine sixes and 10 fours to steer India through a 296-run chase with eight wickets to spare.
Asked what had changed in Kohli’s ODI game, de Villiers said, "I have been following his progress with a lot of interest and it makes me very happy to see the way he's performing, especially keeping in mind that the 2027 World Cup is just around the corner. And what stands out to me is the aggressive nature of his approach these days. It's fantastic to see him using all his experience and realizing to be positive and getting into good positions actually brings out the best in him."
De Villiers, who is set to feature in WCL, which will be broadcast on FanCode, termed Kohli’s current phase his "third peak".
"It's an incredible run of form. We've seen this kind of form in 2012 to 2014 and then again 2016 to 2019 and now this is a third peak for him really taking his game to the next level. And we've often heard him speak about sort of taking his game to the next level, thinking about the game a little bit differently. 
And you can see that in that positive and that aggressive approach he's taking on. So, it makes me very happy to see him perform like he is," de Villiers said.
'Mr 360 degree' is equally excited about the ODI World Cup returning to South Africa for the first time since 2003. He hopes the Proteas can go further this time after failing to reach the semifinals in 2003 and believes their recent ODI series win over world champions Australia is an encouraging sign.
"I think that the cricket is going to be magnificent, as it was in 2003 and hopefully the Proteas will perform better this time than back then. From a performance point of view, it doesn't bring back great memories. But the team really looks strong now. Most of the players are still relatively unknown globally, but I know they have a lot of chemistry. There's a great (team) culture. There's lots of individuals who can win your games of cricket.
 And we showcased it now against Australia, winning a sixth consecutive ODI series win against the Aussies. So, really looking good for the guys and once the World Cup starts, there will be a lot of hype, a lot of attention from the media and the public," de Villiers said.

briefs.headline: Rajasthan Royals star creates history, surpasses Gayle for highest T20 score
briefs.deck: Lhuan-dre Pretorius has made T20 cricket history with his phenomenal score of 188 runs off 79 balls while playing for the Titans against the Knights. This feat breaks Chris Gayle's former record of 175 runs, showcasing Pretorius's exceptional talent as he maintained a striking rate of 237.97. His recent century for South Africa further underscores his remarkable consistency and prowess on the…
briefs.bodyText:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius produced a record-breaking innings on Friday, smashing an unbeaten 188 off just 79 balls for South Africa’s Titans against the Knights in a CSA T20 Challenge fixture.
The 20-year-old left-hander struck 15 fours and 13 sixes as he surpassed the previous highest individual score in T20 cricket, the 175 not out hit by former West Indies star 
Chris Gayle
 for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors India in the 2013 
IPL
.
Pretorius’ breathtaking knock came at a strike rate of 237.97 and powered the Titans to 267 for three from their 20 overs.
Pretorius appeared on course to become the first batter to score 200 in a T20 innings, but ran out of deliveries before reaching the landmark.
His 188 not out now stands as the highest individual score in the 20-over format, ahead of Gayle’s 175 not out, while 
Aaron Finch
’s 172 for Australia against Zimbabwe in 2018 remains the highest score in men’s T20 internationals.
Pretorius’ innings also capped a strong run of form. His previous appearance came for South Africa, when he smashed a 53-ball 101 against Namibia in a T20 international last month.
The young batter has, however, had to contend with injury setbacks during his recent rise.
Highest individual scores in T20 cricket
- Lhuan-dre Pretorius – 188* (Titans vs Knights, October 3, 2026)
- Chris Gayle – 175* (Royal Challengers Bangalore vs Pune Warriors India, April 23, 2013)
- Aaron Finch – 172 (Australia vs Zimbabwe, July 3, 2018)
- Hamza Khan – 164* (Rwanda vs Ivory Coast, May 24, 2026)
Pretorius’ 188* has now rewritten the record books for the highest individual score in T20 cricket.
Pretorius is also part of the Rajasthan Royals squad in the IPL, although opportunities have been limited so far. With the franchise having established left-handed opening options in Yashasvi Jaiswal and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 20-year-old has found it difficult to secure a regular place in the playing XI. His record-breaking knock for the Titans, however, is another reminder of his potential and could put him in the spotlight ahead of the next IPL season.

briefs.headline: I hope it will be an entertaining night for everyone: Ancelotti
briefs.deck: The Italian also backs India’s ambitions of hosting a World Cup
briefs.bodyText:
Brazil national team coach Carlo Ancelotti had words of praise for Indian football ahead of his side’s much-anticipated clash, saying the country’s passion for the sport was encouraging.
“It is an honour for us to be here with the national team. We know what it means to be involved with the national team, not just in football,” Ancelotti told a packed media conference.
Expresses happiness
“We are happy to be here, to play against India and to show the quality of our players. We hope it will be an entertaining night for everyone at the stadium.”
The Italian also backed India’s ambitions of hosting a World Cup.
“The possibility of a World Cup in India would be fantastic. India is trying to compete in football as well, and I hope they can have a happy future in the sport,” he said.
Ancelotti added that the match would help Brazil continue rebuilding as it begins a new cycle.

briefs.bodyText:
Pranavi Urs gives up her three-stroke overnight lead after a triple bogey on the third hole of the final round.
She is one under par through seven holes after a birdie on the sixth, but China’s Yin Ruoning is three under through seven and now leads at 14 under. Pranavi is second on 13 under, with Singapore’s Shannon Tan third at 12 under. Yang Yunseo is fourth on 7 under.
India’s 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod produces a stunning 6-3 win over South Korea’s reigning world and former Olympic champion Kang Chaeyoung to reach the women’s individual semifinal. Kumkum takes the opening set 29-28, briefly sees Kang level at 2-2, then responds to lead 4-2.
Kumkum delivers a 10 in the need of the hour and shocks the archery veteran. She will now face China's Zhu Jingyi in the match that could confirm another medal for India in archery.
